name: Rufous-thighed Kite
rangeDescription: Lowlands of the guianas to northern argentina and all of brazil
description: Small unobtrusive raptor. Adults have a gray body (darker above than below), and rufous thighs and eyes.

name: Orange-cheeked Waxbill
rangeDescription: Senegambia to democratic republic of the congo, northern angola, and northern zambia
description: A tiny finch of grassy areas. Key features include the brown back, red rump, orange face, and bright red bill.

name: Sulu Cuckooshrike
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (sulu archipelago)
description: Sleek but sturdy gray bird, endemic to the Sulu Archipelago, in the southwestern Philippines. Uniform overall, but darker on the tail, wingtips, and between the eye and bill.

name: Crested Ibis
rangeDescription: China (mainly shaanxi, in north-central china); reintroduced into southern south korea (upo wetlands) and sado island, northwestern japan
description: A white, exotic-looking waterbird with a bright red face and raggedy crest. Adults are washed in gray during the breeding season.

name: White-collared Kite
rangeDescription: Atlantic lowland rainforest of northeastern brazil (pernambuco and alagoas)
description: Rather large raptor, mostly black above and white below. Note the mostly white tail with a broad dark band, and the black-and-white bars on the flight feathers.

name: Socorro Wren
rangeDescription: Socorro island (revillagigedo islands off western mexico)
description: Only found on Socorro Island, where it is the only wren. Occurs in woodland, brushy thickets, and scrubby vegetation, often in pairs or family groups.

name: Guadeloupe Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Varied forest types on guadeloupe (central lesser antilles)
description: A medium-sized, shy woodpecker that occupies most wooded habitats including mangrove swamps. This is a striking species, clothed nearly entirely in glossy black, save for the deep crimson belly and chest on many individuals.

name: Velvet-purple Coronet
rangeDescription: Western andes of southwestern colombia and northwestern ecuador
description: This medium-sized hummingbird looks all blackish in poor light, but at the right angle, it turns into a dazzling gem with a purple belly and crown, turquoise sides, and greenish wing coverts. Note bright white flashes in the tail.

name: Littoral Rock-Thrush
rangeDescription: Arid littoral of southwestern madagascar
description: Chunky, mid-sized robin-like bird. Males are pale gray and orange, while females are gray-brown.

name: Rufous Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Alaska to northwestern usa; winters to southern mexico
description: Adult males are almost entirely orange with bright white chest and some green on the back (can be solid green like Allen's Hummingbird). Throat is iridescent, and depending on the light, can look anywhere from red to orange to yellow to lime green.

name: Sulawesi Pygmy Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Sulawesi, togian islands (to northeast) and buton (to southeast)
description: A small brown-and-white woodpecker with scattered pale bars and spots on the upperparts and dark-streaked white underparts. Male possess a red nape patch that is absent in females.

name: Cundinamarca Antpitta
rangeDescription: Eastern andes of colombia (cundinamarca and meta)
description: A rather plain antpitta known only from a small area of Colombia’s eastern Andes, southeast of Bogotá. Plumage is dull brown with small white streaks on the underparts, a slightly paler belly, and a faint eyering.

name: Bronze-winged Jacana
rangeDescription: Lowlands of india to southwestern china, southeastern asia, sumatra, and java
description: Gangly inhabitant of well-vegetated wetlands, especially ponds and lakes with floating vegetation. Adult’s dark neck and bright white eyebrows are unmistakable.

name: Yellow-vented Eremomela
rangeDescription: Southern ethiopia to southern somalia, northeastern uganda, and southeastern kenya
description: A small, drab warbler-like bird of dry country. The upperparts are gray and the underparts pale, with a small amount of yellow on the vent.

name: Tawitawi Brown-Dove
rangeDescription: Tawitawi (sulu archipelago)
description: A medium-sized dove of lowland secondary forest on Tawi-Tawi Island, where it is the only brown-dove. Dark brown above with a gray head, purplish iridescence on the back of the neck, rufous-brown underparts from the throat to the belly, white under the base of the tail, and a pale gray tail tip.

name: Violet-eared Waxbill
rangeDescription: Angola to namibia, zambia, southern zimbabwe, botswana, and northern south africa
description: A stunning long-tailed waxbill with a red bill, mauve cheeks, and a blue rump. The underparts are vibrant chestnut in the male and cream-buff in the female.

name: Chestnut-bellied Hummingbird
rangeDescription: West slope of eastern andes of north-central colombia
description: Endangered hummingbird with a small range in the northern part of Colombia’s eastern Andes and in the San Lucas Mountains. Note the reddish-orange belly and bright rusty tail.

name: Golden Palm Weaver
rangeDescription: Savanna of ethiopia to southern somalia, eastern kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding male is bright yellow with a mostly orange head. The female is duller, though still very yellow.

name: Singing Starling
rangeDescription: New guinea, including aru islands (off southwestern new guinea) to bismarck archipelago and solomon islands
description: Large songbird of New Guinea and Solomon Islands, also on Boigu Island in the northern Torres Strait. Adult glossy black with strong metallic green/blue sheen and bright red eye.

name: Markham's Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds paracas peninsula (peru); ranges to southern mexico and chile
description: Small dark seabird of Humboldt Current, although relatively large for a storm-petrel; not seen from shore, but breeds inland in Atacama Desert where it visits colonies at night to avoid predators. Favors warmer waters beyond cooler inshore zone.
